summary: Configured node1 and node2 (SONiC-VS routers) to exchange each other's private-network prefixes (192.168.10.0/24 behind node1↔node3, 192.168.20.0/24 behind node2↔node4) via iBGP over the eth1 transit link (172.20.1.0/31), extending SONiC's existing AS 65100 FRR instance rather than entering static routes. node3/node4 got static host routes to their own gateway only (normal leaf-host config, not the protocol under test). Verified end-to-end node3↔node4 reachability over the private path, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with boot-id proof and post-restart re-verification of BGP sessions, kernel routes, and connectivity. Discovered and fixed a persistence gap: SONiC's bgp container regenerates FRR config from configdb templates on boot, silently dropping manually-added vtysh neighbors — added a systemd oneshot (apply-transit-bgp.service) on node1/node2 that reapplies the iBGP neighbor/network config once bgpd is ready on every boot; interface IPs and forwarding sysctls were persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/ and /etc/sysctl.d/, and node3/node4's private IP+route via NetworkManager connection profiles.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via IPv6 link-local neighbor discovery: node1.eth1<->node2.eth1 (transit), node1.eth2<->node3.enp8s0, node2.eth2<->node4.enp8s0
Cleaned up SONiC docker0/interface reconcilers on node1 and node2 per platform reference
Enabled global+per-interface IPv4 forwarding on node1 and node2

Extended SONiC's existing AS 65100 FRR instance with an iBGP neighbor between node1 (router-id 10.1.0.1) and node2 (changed router-id to 10.1.0.2 to avoid duplicate-ID conflict), advertising each side's private /24 via network statements
Configured node3 and node4 enp8s0 with static IPs and static routes to reach each other's private subnet via their respective router
Verified node3<->node4 reachability over the private path only (traceroute confirmed hop via 192.168.10.1)
Persisted node1/node2 interface addressing (/etc/network/interfaces.d/), forwarding sysctls (/etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf), and docker0 neutralization (systemd oneshot) so they survive reboot
Persisted node3/node4 private IP+route via nmcli static NetworkManager profile
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, BGP Established state, and private-path connectivity for all 4 nodes
Restarted node3, node4, node1, node2 one at a time via native reboot, confirming boot_id changed and each node's required services/routes recovered before moving to the next

Discovered SONiC's bgp container regenerates FRR config from configdb on boot, wiping manually-added vtysh BGP neighbors; fixed by adding apply-transit-bgp.service (systemd oneshot, After=bgp.service) on node1 and node2 that waits for bgpd readiness and reapplies the iBGP neighbor/network config on every boot
Re-verified BGP sessions Established and node3<->node4 connectivity after all 4 restarts

evidence.requirement: Topology discovery: node1/node2 transit link and node1-node3 / node2-node4 private links identified
evidence.summary: IP/interface survey plus IPv6 link-local neighbor discovery on node1/node2 eth1/eth2 confirms the transit and private-link wiring

evidence.requirement: node1/node2 iBGP session established, private networks learned via BGP (not static)
evidence.summary: vtysh shows BGP Established between 172.20.1.0 and 172.20.1.1 in AS 65100; kernel/FRR RIB shows 192.168.20.0/24 on node1 and 192.168.10.0/24 on node2 with proto bgp

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other over the private-network path (not the shared management network)
evidence.summary: Source-bound pings between 192.168.10.2 and 192.168.20.2 succeed; tracepath from node3 shows the path transiting 192.168.10.1 (node1) then reaching 192.168.20.2

evidence.requirement: Configuration persistence across reboot (interfaces, forwarding, BGP)
evidence.summary: Persistent config written: /etc/network/interfaces.d + sysctl.d + docker0-neutralize.service on node1/node2, nmcli static profiles on node3/node4, and apply-transit-bgp.service to reapply BGP neighbor config every boot (needed after discovering SONiC's template regeneration wipes manual vtysh config)
